tagline: a Kurushi / Intelligent Qube systems study — the grid, the void, the rolling cubes
study: Original recreation of the SYSTEMS of Kurushi Final / Intelligent Qube (Sony, 1997). All art/audio original; original title; no Sony assets, names, or the walking-character design. Original working title: CUBEFALL.
engine: Godot 4.7 GDScript, 3D, PORTRAIT 540x960 phone-first (the grid's long axis runs INTO the screen — waves roll toward the camera from the fog horizon), stretch canvas_items/expand, gl_compatibility, web-first (itch HTML5 plays on phones), Android APK via the arcade pattern later

psx_law.low_res: render at 320x240 into a viewport, upscale nearest-neighbor
psx_law.vertex_wobble: vertex snapping shader (snap to a virtual 160px grid) — the PSX swimming look
psx_law.affine_hint: texture gradient dithering; no filtering (nearest), no AA, no shadows (blob decal under the walker)
psx_law.palette: dark void, steel gray cubes, deep green advantage cubes, matte black forbidden cubes, fog

grid.floor_fall: captured/exited rows drop into the void with tumble

player.kind: the Marker — an abstract glowing figure
player.move: cell-to-cell with input repeat, grid-aligned, mark squares with a rise animation (the classic mark plate)
player.capture: marked squares flash then capture the row when cubes roll over them

cubes.law: normal — capture for score; letting one roll off the far edge into the void SHRINKS the field
forbidden — capturing a black cube = instant game over; blacks must be allowed to roll off safely; they never count toward waves
advantage — capturing one marks a 3x3 area, capturing that area earns bonus + a roll of extra field

roll.law: cubes roll 90° per cell — real 3D rotation around the leading bottom edge, NOT sliding (the feel IS the roll)
roll.waves: rows spawn on a beat, accelerating per stage

capture.perfect_clear: capture EVERY cube in a wave = ABSOLUTE — the whole stage's cubes in that wave captured, big bonus

score.stage_clear: survive N waves with field intact

death: fall into the void (standing on a fallen row)

milestones: 1 GRID CORE: 3D grid + rolling cube math (90° edge roll) + the Marker + mark/capture one row + battery (roll math, capture windows)
2 CUBE LAW: gray/black/green taxonomy + forbidden law + waves + field shrink + perfect-clear
3 RUN: stages, score, HUD, speed ramp, game-over/win, camera drama (the void pull)
4 PSX PASS: low-res + vertex wobble + dither + fog + audio (roll thuds, mark blip, capture crash, absolute fanfare) + export

controls.move: swipe/drag short = step cell-by-cell (grid-aligned, input-repeat on hold); WASD/arrows on desktop
controls.mark: tap the cell in front of the marker (or tap ANY cell within the 3x3 reach law) raises the mark plate
controls.trigger: capture fires when cubes roll over marks — but the phone gets a big CAPTURE button too (the classic trigger), thumb-reachable bottom-right
controls.reach: v1 keeps classic reach: mark the cell ahead only (swipe+tap = the whole grammar)

phone_law.camera: elevated behind-the-marker follow, tilted so the wave horizon sits in the top third; slight dolly-out as field shrinks
phone_law.thumb_rule: all buttons bottom-arc; nothing critical above the midpoint; one-hand playable
phone_law.performance: <=60 draw calls typical (grid = one merged mesh per row state, cubes instanced), 320x240 internal render keeps phones at 60fps in gl_compatibility

art_source_law.textures: Flux (NVIDIA endpoint) + PIL — flat retro textures, same lane as all games
art_source_law.models: CODE-BUILT low-poly only (walker <= 300 tris, cubes are BoxMesh) — the PSX law FORBIDS generated heavy meshes (TRELLIS output is ~100x over budget)
art_source_law.sculmm_lanes: Colab CLI serves THREE fronts for the GMP (PLAN.md P5): (1) MESHES — TRELLIS/Hunyuan shape chains, content-addressed work-orders; (2) ANIMATION — BVH mocap applied to generated meshes via the rigid nearest-segment bind law + clips.json registry (the animated pilot pipeline); (3) CINEMATICS — Blender cel/clay render passes with the spring-arm camera law. CUBEFALL v1 stays code-animated (marker tweens; a 300-tri figure needs no mocap) — the animation lane is for organic characters (RPG cutscenes, STAR VISITOR idle/ride cycles) and title cinematics.
art_source_law.audio: procedural synthesis in code (the arcade SfxManager pattern)
